findings.claim: The Usage settings sheet mutates and persists five Settings-owned policies locally with zero deep-links and zero commands, which is the behaviour core packet 05 names a Hard failure and which reproduces four controls from the Settings owner's own inventory.
findings.detail: u11-prism.html:1099 `sheetHTML()` emits four sections, only one of which is read-only. The three editable sections write policy that reference canon A1.3 [LIVE-CORE] and HERMES_USAGE_HANDOFF.md:28-36 assign to Settings: (a) :1107 `data-u11set="warnLow"` = "model/provider/cache/context warning preferences"; (b) :1108 `data-u11set="autoSwitch"` "Automatic account/provider switching" = "account/provider fallback" policy, and packet 06:64 additionally states "Route resolution and scheduling remain outside Usage"; (c) :1111/:1119 `product` + `after` = "continuation policy"; (d) :1131 `data-u11extra` "Extra paid usage" = "included-plan versus extra-usage behavior"; (e) :1133 `data-u11limit` "Spending limit … $ / month" = the spending guard. The change handler at :1186-1210 writes each to the in-page `settings` object and calls `STORE.set('u11:settings', settings)` (:1193, :1200, :1208) — localStorage. No branch dispatches a command and no branch calls `D.deepLink`; the two `deepLink` calls in the sheet (:1178, :1179) hang off the separate `[data-u11link]` click handler at :1174-1184 and are reachable only from the two footer buttons at :1155-1156, which the user need never press. This is not invented vocabulary: ORIGINAL_SETTINGS_USAGE_HANDOFF.md:145-160 is the Settings-owner control inventory and lists "Automatic account switching" (:151), "Warn me before I run low" (:152, byte-identical to the sheet's label), "Use extra paid usage" (:158) and "Monthly spending limit" (:159). So the sheet duplicates named Settings controls rather than linking to them, which is precisely what ORIGINAL_SETTINGS_USAGE_HANDOFF.md:11 forbids ("must not create a separate settings system") and HERMES_USAGE_HANDOFF.md:48 restates ("Deep-link to semantic Settings destinations"). Enabling paid extra usage and setting a monthly spend cap from the reporting surface also has no confirmation, permission, result or receipt, against packet 06:53-55 and canon A1.59. The sheet trigger is the ungated header button at u11-prism.html:355 (`id="u11Settings"`, no `.u11-advonly`), so every control is reachable at Essentials disclosure. The sheet's own subtitle (:1105) claims it is "a consumer of the shared Settings registry, never a second settings system" and its note (:1158) claims "Widget settings never change these policies"; both are self-certifications the probe contradicts.

findings.claim: The policy the sheet writes is never read by any renderer, so the Usage page keeps reporting the superseded policy as current fact — a user who caps Extra usage at $20 is still told the cap is $100, and a user who enables AI Credit Overages is still told they are off.
findings.detail: An exhaustive grep of the whole bundle shows `settings.warnLow`, `settings.autoSwitch`, `settings.afterIncludedByProduct` and `settings.extraUsage` are read in exactly one place — `sheetHTML()` redrawing its own inputs (u11-prism.html:1107, :1108, :1118, :1130). No widget, no meter, no continuation string and no cost figure consumes them. Meanwhile `renderPlans` (u11-widgets.js:278) prints the static fixture string `d.continuation[p.id].whatHappensNext`. Measured consequence after the five mutations of A01-01: the Plans room text is byte-identical before, after, and after a full reload with the mutated policy still in localStorage; `window.U11.productById['prod:claude-extra'].spendingLimitMicro` is still 100000000, `meter:claude-extra` is still `{used:12.4, limit:100, usedPct:12, note:'User spending limit'}`, and `window.U11.productById['prod:antigravity-overage'].enabled` is still false. So the page simultaneously shows the user's own input of 20 in the sheet and "continue with extra usage up to the $100 spending limit" in the Plans room, and shows "AI Credit Overages" ticked in the sheet and "AI Credit Overages are off" in the Plans room. This is a wrong settlement/limit number and a false certainty presented to the user, and it is also the second half of packet 05's Hard-failure pair — local mutation plus a reporting surface that contradicts it. Note the distinction the method rules require: the mutated value IS in storage (probe `plans-diff-after-reload.persistedSettings`), and the UI renders the OLD value — the defect is precisely that the data and the render disagree.

findings.detail: Packet 01:52-70 requires Usage to "Render adapter-provided choices" under the heading "What happens when included usage runs out?", with a named vocabulary (Stop and wait / Use extra balance / Use a usage pack / Use paid usage after the plan / Use saved reset / Switch account / Switch provider / Use free models / Use API billing / Ask each time), "only when supported". For `prod:claude-max` (order `['included','prod:claude-extra','hard_stop']`) the measured options are `included / Draw on the balance/pack / Stop`. Two defects follow. findings.claim: The only ownership-respecting route from a widget to the Settings owner — the "Open Usage settings" footer button, emitted 27 times — is inert, so the concept's editable in-Usage policy sheet works while its widget-level handoff to the owner does not.
findings.detail: Every widget footer emits `data-u11-act="opensettings"` (u11-widgets.js:184), and the dispatcher at u11-widgets.js:1219-1221 fires `document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('u11:opensettings'))`. There is no listener, so the event is a no-op: measured, the event fires (1 synthetic listener caught it), the settings sheet does not open, and `window.U11.cmdLog` gains nothing. Reported here strictly as the ownership consequence, not as a click-deadness finding — the runtime axis already owns that (its G2 group click-proved 10 of these buttons change nothing and counted 27 in total). On this axis the asymmetry is the point: of the concept's affordances that touch Settings, the four that navigate to the owner are the two sheet footer links (u11-prism.html:1155-1156), the account Reconnect link and the setup link — none of which a user must ever use — while 27 widget-level "go to the owner" buttons are dead and the local policy editor is fully functional. The `u11:opensettings` contract also has no defined owner: it is neither a canonical command (canon A1.58) nor a semantic deep-link destination (canon A1.8), so even a listener would not make it an ownership-respecting route.

findings.detail: PROVIDER_CLI_FINAL_ADJUDICATION.md (precedence 1) specifies the runtime-demand flow as "return Provider Setup Required when none is ready → deep-link to the exact Provider Settings/setup row → preserve originating operation and continuation token", and separately insists installations are "installed for the exact selected Host/Environment". Why the severity is wrong: 04_SERVER_NETWORK_MAINTENANCE_AND_DATA_QUALITY.md:56 requires only that a maintenance flow's model call be 'a separate validation event' (satisfied — ue-609 is bucket validation, purpose probe, joined by validationFor), and §Catalog and probes:104 requires only that probes be attributed as validation/probe Usage (satisfied). PROVIDER_CLI_FINAL_ADJUDICATION.md:26-32 governs binding of the INSTALLATION to the exact host/environment, not which account a verification call bills. ue-609 has requestedAccountId === effectiveAccountId, so no route-divergence rule is breached either. verdicts.corrected_claim: Restate as a fixture-coherence defect, not an attribution-rule violation: the flagship demonstration of the packet's 'maintenance verify is a separate validation event' rule (fixture 13) routes the Codex CLI update's verify step to an unrelated provider — Qwen3-Coder-Plus on conn:opencode-go / acct:opencode-personal, whose 5-hour credit meter sits at 72% — while the Codex CLI's own connection (conn:openai-personal-codex, 'Codex · ChatGPT plan') goes unused, and the inspector shows the Codex-CLI maintenance note and the OpenCode connection/account/product in the same panel with no explanation. Consequences: the verify does not exercise the thing installed, so the adjudication's 'verify provider/model readiness' step is not actually demonstrated; and a reader sees a Codex maintenance flow consuming an unrelated plan's allowance. No cited rule is broken — this is a fixture-realism/explanation gap in the concept's demo data.

verdicts.reason: The mismatch is real and is in fact a triple mismatch. ops-1 is 'Codex CLI update' from the 'official OpenAI installer' bound to host:win-desktop/env:native (u11-data.js:762-765), while its verification attempt ue-609 (u11-data.js:698-705) runs connectionId 'conn:opencode-go' / productId 'prod:oc-go-plan' / model 'model:qwen3-coder-plus' on acct:opencode-personal — and those span three different families (acct:opencode-personal is fam:opencode at u11-data.js:68, model:qwen3-coder-plus is fam:alibaba at u11-data.js:203, while the Codex CLI's own connection conn:openai-personal-codex sits on fam:openai at u11-data.js:83 and is unused). requestedAccountId == effectiveAccountId with no fallbackReason, so it is not a demonstrated fallback. u11-rundetail.js:315-327 then renders the maintenance note and the 'Connection used' block in the same panel with no bridging explanation, exactly as axis8-ops-attribution-probe.json verificationLink.panelText shows. But the cited rules are satisfied, not violated: 04_*.md:56 requires a separate validation event (present), 04_*.md:104 requires probes be attributed as validation/probe Usage (done — bucket 'validation', purpose 'probe'), and ADJ:26-32 binds the post-consent lifecycle to the exact installation/host/environment, which ops-1 records correctly. Nothing in the packet, the adjudication or canon dictates which connection a verification model call must use, or requires the UI to explain the route. The live requirement it actually offends is realistic demo content (canon/01-reference-canon.md A9 item 77, HER:740) — a fixture-authoring coherence defect, not an attribution or settlement error, since the call is correctly attributed to the account that (per the fixture) made it and installer time is correctly kept out of tokens.

Separately, models[] carries only familyId (u11-data.js:198-212), which is the model's vendor, not the family that routes it: fam:opencode, fam:antigravity and fam:github have zero models while all three carry usage, and three freeModels rows route a model through a different family than its registry family (GPT-5.6/fam:openai via fam:github; Qwen3 Coder Plus and Qwen3 Max/fam:alibaba via fam:opencode). findings.claim: u11-time.js rejects any system timezone whose IANA id contains no '/', so on a UTC-configured host every rendered timestamp is silently shifted to America/New_York and labelled EDT — reproduced: the 18:42Z demo instant renders as '14:42 EDT'.
findings.detail: u11-time.js:18-24 accepts Intl's resolved zone only if z.indexOf('/') !== -1, otherwise falls back to the hard-coded FALLBACK_ZONE 'America/New_York'. 'UTC' (the default in containers, on servers, and on the TrueNAS/Docker host this very concept models at u11-data.js:815,819) fails that test even though it is a perfectly determinable system zone. The page then renders every clock four hours early with a confident 'EDT' abbreviation: reset/cooldown lines, 'Started', ledger stamps and forecast 'generated' times. The module computes ZONE_IS_FALLBACK (u11-time.js:25-29) and exports it (u11-time.js:179), but no file in the concept consumes it (grep across all .js/.html: the only hit is the export), so nothing on screen discloses that the zone was guessed. Contrast case: with timezoneId 'Asia/Tokyo' the same page correctly renders '03:42 GMT+9' — the defect is specific to slash-less zone ids, not to non-US zones. The 24-hour requirement itself passes (0 AM/PM matches across all 13 rooms).
evidence: u11-time.js:17-24 — "var FALLBACK_ZONE = 'America/New_York'; … if (z && typeof z === 'string' && z.indexOf('/') !== -1) return z; return FALLBACK_ZONE;"

verdicts.corrected_claim: Two framing corrections. (1) P03:44-58 says 'Separate:' a list of time kinds — it does not require every kind to be a partition of a run's elapsed, and the concept does separate maintenance time (u11-data.js:766 Check 2m / Wait for idle 9m / Install 3m / Verify 4m / Rollback 1m) and outbox/offline time (u11-data.js:772) in the operations surface; so 'never carries Maintenance at all' must be stated as 'never inside a run's time decomposition', which is how the detail already reads. (2) The one clear 'Separate:' violation is the local-compute / tool-runtime merge at u11-data.js:857 — those two kinds are separated nowhere in the concept (the 'Local compute' label at u11-rundetail.js:299 is an attachment property with value 'none', not a time). The remainder — the dropped 'snapshot' token, two zero-valued kinds, and two of three runs with timing:null — is coverage thinness rather than a rule breach.

The live formulation of this requirement merges exactly the two rows the finding says must be split: canon item 69 (01-reference-canon.md:127, LIVE-CORE, citing SEC:346-356 AND P03:44-58) lists 'local tool/runtime time' as one kind, and SECOND_USAGE_HANDOFF.md:352 does the same while prefacing the list with 'Detailed run views may distinguish'. findings.detail: ops-8 is the runtime-demand fixture: "Codex CLI requested on Home Server · not installed", hostId host:truenas, envId env:docker. Its setupLink is the entire representation of ADJ:44. The payload is {surface:'settings', manager:'providers', section:'setup', focus_reason:'setup_required', continuation:'cont-8841'} — five keys, none of which name a provider family, a CLI, an account, a connection, a host, or an environment. I clicked "Open provider setup" at runtime and captured the payload from U11.cmdLog: byte-identical to the literal, and a regex for /openai|codex|host:|env:|ops-8/i over the captured payload returns no match. The same payload would be produced for any provider CLI on any host, so a real Settings surface receiving it could only open the generic Providers > setup list. Canon A8 (`HER:687-698`, `SEC:403`, marked LIVE-CORE) lists the destination as (surface, manager, provider_family_id, account_id?, connection_id?, product_id?, model_id?, section ∈ {usage_and_extra_usage, routing, models, diagnostics}, setting_id?, focus_reason) — provider_family_id is not optional, and 'setup' is not in the canonical section enum. All five deep-link payloads in the concept omit provider_family_id; the reconnect payload at u11-widgets.js:1224-1225 does at least carry account_id, which makes the setup payload strictly the least precise of the set even though it is the one the adjudication is most specific about. findings.claim: The "After included usage → Then" control in the Usage settings sheet displays a wrong continuation for 9 of 12 products — it renders the literal token "included" as the answer to what happens after included usage, and silently discards the seeded 'credits' and 'extra_usage' preferences because the option keys can never match them.
findings.detail: u11-prism.html:1082-1097 builds the option list by collapsing each continuation order step to a coarse key: any 'prod:*' step becomes 'prod', any 'fallback:*' becomes 'fallback', everything else keeps its literal token; a `seen[key]` dedupe then drops every subsequent step sharing a key. u11-prism.html:1118 selects with `o === cur || key === cur`, falling back to opts[0]. Measured at runtime across all 12 continuation products (fresh localStorage, u11:settings.selectedProduct seeded per product, sheet opened): (a) prod:codex-plus has stored preference 'credits' (u11-data.js:1162) but the option keys are included/prod/wait_reset, so nothing matches and the select displays "included"; (b) prod:claude-max has stored 'extra_usage' and likewise displays "included"; (c) only prod:oc-go-plan ('free_fallback') matches and displays "Continue with free models"; (d) for the 9 products whose order starts with 'included' and that have no stored preference, the displayed value is also the literal "included"; (e) prod:oc-zen-balance displays the raw token "balance". So the flagship question the packet §05 requires the default view to answer — "What will happen next?" — is answered "included" for the Codex plan whose real policy is "use credits up to $20 this month". Two further consequences: the `credits: 'Use credits'` and `saved_reset: 'Apply the saved reset'` labels at u11-prism.html:1086-1088 are unreachable dead code (credits/saved-reset arrive as 'prod:' steps), and codex-plus's four-step chain (included → credits → saved reset → wait reset) collapses to three options that merge credits and the saved reset into one generic "Draw on the balance/pack", losing the order the data specifies. None of the nine rendered strings matches canon B-I-7's required continuation-choice set (Stop and wait / Use extra balance / Use a usage pack / Use paid usage after the plan / Use saved reset / Switch account / Switch provider / Use free models / Use API billing / Ask each time) — zero exact matches — which is a terminology-axis lead but is what makes the wrong value unrecognisable as wrong.

findings.claim: The registers claim "every policy action deep-links to Settings", but the 27 most prominent settings affordances in the UI are not deep links at all, and impact-register.json's settings_deep_links inventory omits the setup destination that the correction packet added.
findings.detail: footActs (u11-widgets.js:177-187) puts a "Open Usage settings" button in every widget footer; the handler at u11-widgets.js:1219-1222 dispatches a CustomEvent 'u11:opensettings' and returns. findings.claim: There is no URL addressability anywhere in the concept — zero location.hash, hashchange, pushState or replaceState — so no deep link is re-enterable, bookmarkable, or assertable by URL, and every one of the five deep links terminates in a toast.
findings.detail: Confirmed by grep across u11-prism.html, u11-data.js, u11-widgets.js, u11-context.js, u11-rundetail.js, u11-time.js and _shared/*.js: no location.hash, no 'hashchange', no pushState/replaceState, no URLSearchParams. The single URL-reading site in the whole bundle is _shared/usage-chrome.js:205, `var EMBED = /(\?|&)embed=1(&|$)/.test(window.location.search)` — I verified ?embed=1 does take effect (top chrome hidden), so exactly one piece of state is URL-addressable and it is not a fixture, a room, a scope, a disclosure level, or a deep-link destination. I also set location.hash='#pane=ledger' at runtime: the active pane stayed 'overview'. findings.claim: Disclosure has no effect on which widgets mount: the mounted-type list is byte-identical at Essentials, Standard and Advanced, so the Advanced-only 'Source authority' widget mounts at Essentials and the rail-hidden Source authority room renders in full.
findings.detail: Mechanism, verified in source and matching the measurement: `typesForRoom()` (u11-prism.html:599-602) does filter the room's declared types by `U11W.typesForDisclosure[disclosure]` (u11-widgets.js:37-43), but the filtered list is then passed to `PMWidgets.mount` alongside `defaultBoard: BOARDS[pageId]` (u11-prism.html:630). In the engine, `seedItems(types, board)` prefers the board whenever one exists (_shared/usage-widgets.js:108-110) and `boardItems(board)` filters only by `typeKnown(b.type)` (_shared/usage-widgets.js:98-107) — the canvas's `types` never constrain the curated board. `load()` has the same gap for stored layouts (_shared/usage-widgets.js:111-129) and `resetCanvas()` re-seeds from the same board (_shared/usage-widgets.js:621), so a board saved at Advanced also survives a drop to Essentials. The only place `pmw.types` is consumed is the Add-widget picker (_shared/usage-widgets.js:303). The one-line fallback at u11-prism.html:630 (`types.length ? types : roomTypes.slice(0,1)`) would defeat the filter even if the board were removed: for `u11-authority` the first declared type is `authority` itself. Consequence: at Essentials 12 out-of-level widget types mount (authority in plans/accounts/free/authority, analytics in costs/analytics, cache in context/cache, runs+operations in ledger, tools, signals) and the Source authority room renders 1,233 characters with 1 card and the heading 'Source authority' — while that very widget prints 'Route snapshots, receipt refs, pricing versions and source authority live here — never in the Essentials view' (u11-widgets.js:955). The rail tab itself is correct (essentials:false / standard:false / advanced:true once the collapsed 'More' group is expanded), so only widget mounting ignores disclosure.

findings.claim: The concept preloads 8 Google Font families from fonts.googleapis.com, so on an offline or air-gapped box 5 of 8 silently fall back to system fonts with no error surfaced — and no run by anyone has yet measured text fitting with the intended fonts loaded.
findings.detail: u11-prism.html:9-12 issues `preconnect` to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com plus a `preload as=style` for Cal Sans, Inter, JetBrains Mono, Nunito, Outfit, Quicksand, Rajdhani and Sora, with a `<noscript>` stylesheet fallback — a remote-origin dependency in a page whose production target is a Slint 1.17.1 desktop app with no browser font CDN (canon A9-81 forbids Web-only assumptions; CR:9 requires local Hub testing). Failure mode measured: with no network the stylesheet request completes with transferSize 0, Chromium raises no `requestfailed`, and Inter, Nunito, Outfit, Rajdhani and Sora do not resolve while Quicksand, JetBrains Mono and Cal Sans do — the page renders in fallback metrics with zero console output. Two consequences. (1) Evidentiary: the 8-theme x 8-width clipped-text arm (0 violations in 80/80 cells) is valid for fallback metrics only, and the concept's own harness cannot detect the shortfall because u11-verify.mjs:94-99 discards any console error whose text merely matches /fonts\.g(oogleapis|static)\.com/ and counts only `msg.type()==='error'` plus pageerror — never failed requests. So `consoleErrors: 0` in the shipped report must not be read as 'no resource failed to load'. (2) Coverage: the replay that did have live font egress (122 font faces, 0 failed requests) ran the concept's own harness, which asserts no text geometry at all — so production text fitting with Inter/Sora/Rajdhani applied is unmeasured by every run to date, in both directions.

findings.claim: The fixture assigns the SAME number (96.8) to the context-ring cache hit and to the Claude CLI connection's provider cache hit, while both surfaces carry copy insisting the two metrics are distinct — so the demo cannot demonstrate the distinction it asserts, and the reader instead sees 96.8% against 97%, a rounding artefact where the copy promises two different facts.
findings.detail: u11-data.js:1078 attaches the note "Context-ring metric distinct from this provider figure" to a row whose `hit` is 96.8, and the cache widget closes with "These are per-provider prompt-cache figures — distinct from the context-ring cache metric" (u11-widgets.js:897); thread t-88's `context.cacheHitRate` is also 96.8 on the same connection (`effectiveConnectionId: 'conn:claude-work-cli'`). The concept therefore states a semantic separation twice and then supplies one number for both sides of it. Because of A05-15 the two renderings differ only by rounding (96.8% vs 97%), which is the single most confusing outcome available: a reader checking the claim finds a 0.2-point discrepancy and can reasonably conclude the "distinction" is a display bug. A fixture that used visibly different values would have made the claim testable.

findings.claim: cmd.account.select_profile is dispatched for a page-scope view filter, but its canonical production contract declares effect_kind "event" with expected_event_types ["account_switch_event"], so a filter click would append durable append-only account-switch history that never happened.
findings.detail: u11-prism.html:940, inside applyScope(), does D.dispatch('cmd.account.select_profile', { scope: window.U11W.pageScope }). The scope value is not an account: U11.scopeNode (u11-data.js:1233-1241) resolves scope ids to kinds 'all', 'comparison', 'family', 'account', 'connection', 'product' and 'meter', so the payload can be 'scope:all', 'cmp:coding-sprint', 'fam:openai' or a meter id, and it carries no profile identity at all. It is the ONLY one of the concept's fourteen reused canonical commands with a non-empty expected_event_types — and it is the one the concept misbinds. findings.detail: Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md:8304 states "cmd.provider.switch_route is adopted verbatim from the FinalGUISpec.md CTA Card Contracts rate_limit row (`provider_id`, `retry_after_ms`)", :8309 defines it as 'Accepts a provider re-route, preferring an alternate provider/plan until the quota window resets; carries provider_id and retry_after_ms context' with the availability guard `alternate_route_available`, and FinalGUISpec.md:28909 is the source row. u11-widgets.js:1231 dispatches window.U11.dispatch('cmd.provider.switch_route', { accountId: acctId }) — no provider_id, no retry_after_ms, an account identity instead, and no representation of the alternate_route_available guard or the five disabled reasons. candidate-command-delta.json's verdict is 'reused-canonical' with rationale 'Reused verbatim for "Use next"'; impact-register.json:78-81 records disposition 'reused'. The semantic reuse for the at-limit fallback case is defensible (fixture 3 is a Work-account-at-limit fallback), but 'verbatim' is not: the payload contract adopted verbatim into Plans is not the payload the concept sends, and the register asserts equivalence without noting the divergence.

findings.claim: Displayed token totals add cache_read (and a reasoning term) onto input+output with no counting_semantics declared anywhere, which is GUI-USG-007's MUST_NOT `cache_added_when_provider_inclusive` / `double_counted_total`, and the same page already loads a shared module that implements the correct rule.
findings.detail:
Two live code paths sum buckets into one number:
(1) u11-widgets.js:685 and :690-691 — `var tot = col[1] + col[2] + col[3] + col[4]` over the series ['input','output','reasoning','cacheRead'] (u11-data.js:1115), used both for stacked bar-height normalisation (:685-686) and for the visible tooltip `title="' + col[0] + ' · ' + tot + 'k tokens"` (:691).
(2) u11-rundetail.js:194 — `t.tokens += (a.tokens.input||0) + (a.tokens.output||0) + (a.tokens.cacheRead||0) + (a.tokens.reasoning||0)`, rendered at :201-202 as "<count> · <tokens> tokens" per bucket in every run-detail panel. Its dead twin is U11.bucketTotals at u11-data.js:1370 (0 call sites — see A04-18).
Arithmetic, by hand from the shipped data:
- run:plan-12 → rendered "Main work / 1 · 85.4k tokens" = ue-570 input 51,200 + output 4,100 + cacheRead 30,100 = 85,400. A 30,100-token cache-read bucket is added into a total for a single attempt.
- run:plan-12 → rendered "Research, attachments & media / 5 · 71.4k tokens" = 26,000 + 22,200 + 18,500 + 0 + 4,720 = 71,420, of which 900 is ue-606's cacheRead added back on an Alibaba route.
- analytics 24h column '14' → rendered "14 · 56k tokens" = 28 + 7 + 3 + 18 (input + output + reasoning + cacheRead).
Across all 45 attempts the formula yields 870,880 tokens versus 689,880 for input+output alone: 181,000 cache-read tokens are added into totals. Per family the overstatement, if cache is a subset of input, is claude +34.5% (72,500 cacheRead on 209,980 in+out), openai +34.0% (69,500 on 204,640), kimi +25.1% (36,600 on 145,650), alibaba +2.0% (2,400 on 117,180). cacheWrite (7,300 tokens on ue-501/ue-560/ue-590) is added by no formula, so the same code both over- and under-counts buckets.
Nothing licenses the addition: 0 of 45 attempts carry counting_semantics, it is absent from reports/event-schema-delta.json's attempt_schema.core.tokens, and a rendered-text sweep of all 13 room panes found 0 occurrences of "counting" or "counting_semantics".
The concept contradicts itself in-repo: u11-prism.html:552 loads `_shared/usage-data.js`, whose SEM table at :76-88 declares 'Codex · ChatGPT plan', 'Codex · API key', Copilot, Cursor and OpenCode as `cache_in_input: 'inclusive'`, whose `sourceAwareTotal()` at :103-113 adds cacheRead ONLY when `cache_in_input === 'additive'`, and which even ships display copy at :594 ("cache is a subset of input — not added"). The correct rule is loaded into the page and the u11 render path ignores it.

verdicts.reason: Mechanism confirmed at every cited location. u11-widgets.js:685 and :690-691 are exactly `var tot = col[1] + col[2] + col[3] + col[4];` over series ['input','output','reasoning','cacheRead'] (u11-data.js:1114), used for bar-height max and the visible `title="' + col[0] + ' · ' + tot + 'k tokens"'`. u11-rundetail.js:194 is exactly `t.tokens += (a.tokens.input||0)+(a.tokens.output||0)+(a.tokens.cacheRead||0)+(a.tokens.reasoning||0)`, reached from :177 `html += bucketHTML(atts)` and rendered at :200-201. Dead twin at u11-data.js:1370 confirmed — `grep -n bucketTotals` returns only the definition at u11-data.js:1363, zero call sites. Arithmetic reproduced from the shipped data: run:plan-12 main bucket = 85,400 (51,200+4,100+30,100), research = 71,420, and analytics 24h col '14' = 28+7+3+18 = 56. Ledger-wide input+output = 689,880 vs +cacheRead = 870,880, i.e. 181,000 cacheRead added; cacheWrite total 7,300 added by no formula. `grep -rn 'counting_semantics|countingSemantics' u11-*.js u11-prism.html` returns nothing, and `grep -in 'subset|inclusive|exclusive' u11-*.js u11-prism.html` returns nothing — no disclosure exists. _shared/usage-data.js:80 does declare 'Codex · ChatGPT plan' cache_in_input:'inclusive', :108 adds cache only when 'additive', :594 ships the 'is a subset of input — not added' copy, and u11-prism.html:552 loads it. GUI-USG-007 MUST_NOT `cache_added_when_provider_inclusive`/`double_counted_total` verified at canon/02-plans-canon.md:329.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Two precision fixes. (1) The per-family overstatement table wrongly indicts Claude: _shared/usage-data.js:77 declares 'Claude' cache_in_input:'additive', so adding cacheRead on Anthropic routes is the correct behaviour under the concept's own table. The demonstrable double-count is the non-Anthropic portion — openai 69,500, kimi 36,600, alibaba 2,400 = 108,500 of the 181,000 (kimi/alibaba fall through semFor()'s default at :99, which is 'inclusive'). Drop 'claude +34.5%' from the table. (2) _shared/usage-data.js is the u1–u10 dataset (window.USAGE); u11's renderers never reference it (`grep -n 'window.USAGE' u11-widgets.js u11-prism.html u11-context.js u11-rundetail.js` → 0 hits). So it is evidence the correct rule was authored in-repo and on the same page, not evidence of a bypassed dependency — state it that way.

verdicts.reason: Code and arithmetic confirmed personally. u11-widgets.js:685 and :690-691 both read `var tot = col[1] + col[2] + col[3] + col[4];` over series ['input','output','reasoning','cacheRead'] (u11-data.js:1114) and render it as the visible `title="' + col[0] + ' · ' + tot + 'k tokens"`; u11-rundetail.js:194 sums input+output+cacheRead+reasoning into the rendered bucket rows at :201-202. My own recomputation over the shipped array: input+output = 689,880, cacheRead = 181,000, total by the shipped formula = 870,880; cacheWrite 7,300 is summed by no formula. counting_semantics is 0/45 (my census), absent from reports/event-schema-delta.json attempt_schema.core.tokens (I dumped it: only input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite/reasoning), and 0 hits for 'counting' across the 13-room rendered corpus. ue-501 (u11-data.js:330) is `prod:codex-plus` with input 42100 / cacheRead 18000, i.e. exactly the route _shared/usage-data.js:79-80 declares `cache_in_input: 'inclusive'`. GUI-USG-007's MUST list and MUST_NOT `cache_added_when_provider_inclusive`/`double_counted_total` are quoted correctly (canon/02-plans-canon.md:326-330), the fixture matrix is live UF-088 canon, and the Usage surface is the concept's own owner scope — no supersession applies (canon/01-reference-canon.md section C lists none).
verdicts.corrected_claim: Two live paths (u11-widgets.js:685/690 and u11-rundetail.js:194) sum input+output+reasoning+cacheRead into rendered token figures while no counting_semantics / input_total_includes_cache / output_total_includes_reasoning / provider_total_semantics field exists anywhere (0/45 attempts, absent from reports/event-schema-delta.json, 0 rendered occurrences) — GUI-USG-007's entire MUST list unmet. Two corrections to the finding's detail: (1) the per-family overstatement table should not be read as claiming all four families are double-counted — the concept's own _shared/usage-data.js:75/82-84 declares Claude and Gemini `cache_in_input: 'additive'`, so adding cacheRead on the claude (72,500) and google routes is the correct treatment; the demonstrable double-counts are the openai/Codex routes (69,500 cacheRead, declared `inclusive` at _shared/usage-data.js:78-80) plus kimi (36,600) and alibaba (2,400), which fall to `semFor()`'s inclusive default at _shared/usage-data.js:98. (2) `_shared/usage-data.js` is loaded at u11-prism.html:552 but no u11 file references `window.USAGE` (grep returns 0 hits in u11-prism.html/u11-data.js/u11-widgets.js) — it is the shared library for the sibling u1–u10 concepts, so 'the page already loads the correct rule and u11 ignores it' is true as a script-tag fact but is not an in-page self-contradiction. The load-bearing violation stands on its own: no semantics declared, so neither the additive nor the inclusive reading is licensed, and the rendered totals commit to additive uniformly.

auditor_correction_2026_08_18.what_was_wrong: The finding's worked example and headline figure were both overstated. It asserted that ue-570 rendering 85.4k was a double-count, and that 181,000 cache-read tokens were added into totals across the 45 attempts. Both assumed cache read is INCLUSIVE of the input bucket for every provider.
auditor_correction_2026_08_18.what_is_true: _shared/usage-data.js:77-88 publishes per-provider counting semantics, and cache_in_input is 'additive' for Claude, Claude Code, Gemini Direct, Antigravity CLI and Gemini Workspace — those providers bill cache read as its own bucket, so adding it is CORRECT. ue-570 runs on acct:claude-work / prod:claude-max (u11-data.js), an additive route, so its 85.4k was right all along.
auditor_correction_2026_08_18.corrected_magnitude: Measured during remediation: the honest total across 45 attempts is 762,380 against the old formula's 870,880 — 108,500 tokens of real inflation, not 181,000. It is concentrated in the inclusive and unpublished-semantics routes: Codex 221,140 -> 151,640, Kimi 182,250 -> 145,650, Alibaba 119,580 -> 117,180. Claude, Gemini and Antigravity totals correctly do not move.

findings.claim: The Analytics room's token series are hard-coded synthetic arrays that reconcile with no usage event: the Reasoning band shows 7k–57k tokens while 0 of 45 attempts carry tokens.reasoning, and the 7d chart asserts 309,120 more tokens than the entire event ledger contains.
findings.detail:
U11.analytics.chart (u11-data.js:1116-1127) is a literal array of columns; nothing derives it from U11.attempts and no drill-through exists from a bar to an event. Measured against the ledger (demo clock NOW = 2026-08-04T18:42:00Z):
- 5h: chart total 151,000 tokens (24+35+18+43+31 k). Attempts started within 5h: 40, totalling 817,880 (input+output+cacheRead). Ratio 0.18×.
- 24h: chart total 327,000 against the same 40 attempts / 817,880. Ratio 0.40×.
- 7d: chart total 1,180,000 (190+223+172+246+81+65+203 k) against the whole 45-event ledger of 870,880. Ratio 1.44× — 309,120 tokens that no event can account for.
The ratios move in opposite directions across windows (0.18× at 5h, 1.44× at 7d), which is direct evidence the series are unrelated to the event data rather than merely mis-scaled.
The reasoning band specifically: the legend renders "Reasoning" (u11-widgets.js:656), the pane copy at u11-prism.html:460 promises "Input, output, reasoning and cache-read traffic stacked", and the chart supplies 7,000 / 14,000 / 57,000 reasoning tokens for 5h / 24h / 7d. Zero of the 45 attempts carry a `tokens.reasoning` field (verified in the live page), so the two event-level formulas that try to include it (u11-rundetail.js:194 live, u11-data.js:1370 dead) always add 0, and u11-rundetail.js:398 (`if (t.reasoning != null) parts.push(… + ' reasoning')`) never fires. Consequence: a user sees 14,000 reasoning tokens for the last 24h in the Analytics room and 0 reasoning tokens on every attempt in the Ledger, Context Details and attempt inspector, with no reconciliation path. reports/event-schema-delta.json declares `tokens.reasoning: "int | omitted"` but no fixture exercises it and the register does not flag it unfixtured, in contrast to its explicit `billing_route_enum.not_yet_fixtured` list.

findings.claim: The concept has no counting_semantics field at all and only 5 of the 11 canonical CV-196 token buckets, so GUI-USG-007's entire MUST list is unrepresented and every parallel per-bucket figure the UI shows is uninterpretable.
findings.detail:
GUI-USG-007 (canon/02-plans-canon.md:326-330) requires `counting_semantics`, `input_total_includes_cache`, `output_total_includes_reasoning` and `provider_total_semantics` on the Usage, Ledger, Runtime Artifacts and model-row surfaces. None exists here:
- 0 of 45 attempts carry any of the four (census in scratchpad/axis4/a3-final.js).
- reports/event-schema-delta.json `attempt_schema.core.tokens` declares exactly five buckets — input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, reasoning — and no semantics field. `input_non_cached`, `output_visible`, `provider_total`, `context_estimate` and `counting_semantics` are all absent, against CV-196's negative constraint "Canonical token buckets must not be collapsed into a smaller field set."
- A rendered-text sweep of all 13 room panes plus the attempt and run drawers found 0 occurrences of "counting", "provider total", or any inclusive/exclusive statement.
Consequence for the user: the attempt inspector renders four parallel numbers — for ue-501, "42.1k in · 3.2k out · 18.0k cache read · 2.4k cache write" — with nothing stating whether the 18.0k sits inside the 42.1k. Depending on the answer the call consumed either 45,300 or 63,300 tokens, a 40% spread, and the concept renders both readings: the run-detail bucket rows and analytics totals take the additive reading while _shared/usage-data.js:80 declares this exact route inclusive.
The gap escapes the concept boundary: the "usage records" export at u11-prism.html:1328-1334 emits canonical UsageRecord field names (`usage_event_id`, `settlement_status`, `source_class`, `cost_microdollars`) with `tokens: a.tokens` and no counting_semantics, so a downstream consumer cannot compute a total without guessing; the CSV export at :1316-1323 additionally drops cache_write entirely. CV-196 acceptance criterion: "Consumers do not collapse the token buckets into a smaller canonical set or double-count provider-inclusive cache/reasoning buckets."

findings.claim: The Ledger turn card presents ONE attempt's token figures as the logical work item's usage; for work-3 the chosen representative is the interrupted attempt, so the card shows 13% of that turn's input, and no turn-level total exists anywhere in the UI.
findings.detail:
renderLedger picks `main = attempts.filter(a => a.bucket === 'main')[0] || attempts[0]` (u11-widgets.js:751) and renders that single attempt's route (:762) and that single attempt's tokens (:763-767) directly under the turn's title. Headline-vs-truth for the 12 rendered cards (input tokens):
- work-3 "Redirect: rewrite rate limiter": headline ue-520, status **interrupted** → 6,200 in / 400 out / 0 cache. Turn truth: 48,700 in / 3,560 out / 23,800 cache. Headline = 13% of turn input. The completed, resumed attempt ue-521 (38,400 / 2,900 / 22,000) is demoted to one of "2 helper calls".
- work-11 "Branch: retry on Claude": 21,900 headline vs 66,000 turn → 33%.
- work-10 "Checkout service audit": 61,000 vs 153,600 → 40%. work-9 crew: 14,200 vs 35,500 → 40%. work-8: 51,200 vs 124,800 → 41%. work-6: 47%. work-7: 53%. work-1: 42,100 vs 63,800 → 66%.
10 of 12 cards under-state their turn's input; the two that match are single-attempt works. No aggregate token figure for a logical work item exists on any surface: the Ledger shows the representative attempt only, the attempt drawer lists each attempt separately, Context Details lists each attempt separately (u11-context.js:378-389), and the only summed figures anywhere are the per-run bucket rows in run detail — which cover the 3 runs, not the 9 turns/thread requests.
Packet 02 permits aggregation ("Default UI may aggregate helpers into understandable groups") but not substitution of one attempt's numbers for the group's, and "Each real attempt is independently attributable and grouped under one logical turn" is defeated when the group's headline is a discarded partial.

findings.detail:
u11-widgets.js:752-753 computes `helpers = attempts.length - 1` and `subagents = attempts.filter(a => a.subagent).length` — two overlapping sets, both also overlapping the headline attempt — and renders them additively at :764-767. Counts as rendered:
- work-7 (2 attempts): "1 helper call · 2 subagents" → 1 headline + 1 + 2 = 4 labels for 2 attempts. The subagent count includes the headline ue-560 and re-counts ue-561, which is already the "1 helper call".
- work-8 (7 attempts): "6 helper calls · 4 subagents" → 11 for 7. work-9 (5): "4 helper calls · 4 subagents" → 9 for 5. work-1 (8): "7 helper calls · 1 subagent" → 9 for 8.
Separately, "helper call" is applied to every non-representative attempt regardless of purpose. Of the 30 so labelled: 4 are purpose:'user_work' primaries — ue-510 (failed primary), ue-521 (the completed resumed primary), ue-592 (the second primary after the model switch), ue-611 (the Extra-Bundle primary); 11 are subagent, 5 crew_member, 2 bsd, 3 conversation_replay, 1 fallback_attempt, 2 probe, 2 moa_*. findings.detail:
Field census over all 45 attempts: `parentEventId` 0/45, `logicalTurnId` 0/45, `attemptId` 0/45, `dedupeKey` 0/45. The only downward link is `subagent.child` (11/45), whose values are run-member handles ('child-47-1', 'plan-12-ext-1', 'crew-3-m1') that point into runs[].members[], not up to a parent event. Concretely unlinked pairs the packet expects to be linked:
- ue-503 (subagent) → its parent primary ue-501: no link.
- ue-521 (resumed) → ue-520 (interrupted): related only by shared workId and a `redirect` object on each side.

findings.claim: Three rows in attempts[] are queued placeholders that made no provider call, so every count derived from attempts[] over-states real provider attempts by three, and one surface renders "1 · 0 tokens" for a call that never happened.
findings.detail:
ue-574, ue-583 and ue-584 carry `tokens: {}`, `startedAt: null`, `effectiveAccountId: null`, `effectiveModelId: null`, `settlement: 'unknown'`, `sourceClass: 'unknown'`, and the dataset's own notes say "Queued — no provider attempt yet" (u11-data.js:497, 532) and "Reducer/synthesis reserved until members finish" (:540). They are nevertheless rows in attempts[], so:
- the Source authority room renders "unknown / 3 / events" as a fourth source class, and the four rows sum to 18 + 1 + 23 + 3 = 45 "events" where only 42 provider attempts exist (u11-widgets.js:925-932 counts `d.attempts` by sourceClass and labels the value "events").
- run detail renders "5 ATTEMPTS" for run:crew-3 (3 real calls) and "7 ATTEMPTS" for run:plan-12 (6 real) via u11-rundetail.js:176.
- the same panel renders "Synthesis & verification / 1 · 0 tokens" for the queued reducer ue-584 — a zero for a call that has not occurred, where the Ledger row and the attempt drawer both correctly render "no provider usage". UF-085 negative constraint: "Do not display missing, disabled, unsupported, blocked, stale, or unknown cost/quota as zero."
- the turn card's helper/subagent counts (A04-05) include them: work-9's "4 helper calls" counts two queued non-attempts.
Packet 02's opening rule is "One provider attempt per event"; modelling a not-yet-dispatched member as a usage event breaks the 1:1 and makes every event count a mixture of calls and reservations.

findings.claim: Mixed-provider work items are collapsed under one attempt's provider in the Ledger turn card and Context Details, directly contradicting the dataset's own rule note that a mixed-provider Crew is "never collapsed under one member's provider".
findings.detail:
`attemptRouteLabel(main)` renders the representative attempt's model/account/product as the work item's route (u11-widgets.js:762, helper at :712-724), and u11-context.js:378-379 repeats the pattern for the Context Details message list. Family spread per rendered card:
- work-9 crew_step: 4 families (claude, alibaba, kimi, openai) collapsed to "Claude Sonnet 4.6 · Claude · Work · Claude Max plan". u11-data.js:896 states, for this exact run, `note: 'Mixed-provider Crew — never collapsed under one member's provider.'`
- work-1: 6 families (openai, alibaba, kimi, google, claude, opencode) → "GPT-5.6-Codex · OpenAI · Personal · ChatGPT plan".
- work-8: 3 families → "Claude Opus 4.6 · Claude · Work · Claude Max plan". work-10: 2 → "GPT-5.6-Codex · OpenAI · Personal · ChatGPT plan". work-2, work-4, work-6 likewise.
7 of 12 rendered cards attribute multi-provider work to a single provider on their face. The run-detail panel does render each Crew member's own route correctly, so the defect is confined to the Ledger and Context surfaces — but those are the defaults, and Essentials/Standard users never see the expanded rows, because renderLedger only emits per-attempt rows when `U11W.disclosure === 'advanced'` (u11-widgets.js:741, 769).

findings.claim: Four packet-required route fields are carried by only 3 of 45 attempts, and the concept's own register reclassifies all of them as "optional_existing".
findings.detail:

findings.detail:

The defect is that the exclusion is total — bsd-3 is excluded from rendering too. The only render path for a bsdEvent is keyed by an attempt's eventId and there is no attempt to open. A text sweep of all 13 room panes found 0 occurrences of "Duplicate suppressed" or "duplicate_suppressed", and a grep of every renderer (u11-widgets.js, u11-prism.html, u11-rundetail.js, u11-context.js, _shared/*.js) finds no reference to `duplicate_suppressed` and, case-insensitively, no reference to "bsd" outside u11-rundetail.js. The user is never shown that a duplicate BSD call was suppressed with zero additional usage, which packet 02's BSD record list requires.
Register defect: reports/demo-fixture-report.json fixture 11 lists all three bsdEvents including "bsd-3 duplicate_suppressed (eventId null — zero usage)" against a single `ui_path` of "Ledger · validation bucket · attempt inspector 'Back Seat Driver' section" — which does not exist for bsd-3 — and marks it "pass". findings.claim: Exactly one of the 18 required purpose values — catalog_validation — has no event in the data; no renderer would show an empty group for it, because grouping is by bucket and purpose is humanised inline.
findings.detail:
Direct answer to the axis question. The data uses 17 purpose values across 45 attempts: user_work 14, subagent 8, crew_member 5, conversation_replay 3, bsd 2, probe 2, and one each of approval_review, attachment_transform, compression, fallback_attempt, mcp_router, moa_aggregator, moa_reference, skill_search, title_generation, vision, web_extract. Against packet 02's 18-value minimum the single missing value is **catalog_validation**; there are no extra values outside the required set.
No renderer would show an empty group for it. There is no purpose enum or label map anywhere in the concept — every consumer humanises the raw value inline: u11-widgets.js:779 (ledger attempt row), u11-rundetail.js:234 (attempt block), u11-context.js:385 (Context Details row). findings.claim: The "After included usage → Then" control collapses five distinct product kinds into one label, silently DROPS the Extra Bundle (purchased_pack) and the Saved reset (saved_reset) steps entirely via a key-collapse dedupe, and renders raw enum tokens ("included", "balance") as the default answer for 11 of 12 policies.
findings.detail: afterIncludedOptions normalizes every 'prod:*' step to the single key 'prod' and every 'fallback:*' to 'fallback', then dedupes on the normalized key. Consequences, all measured against the real UI: (1) Coding Plan's order ['included','prod:alibaba-ptp','prod:alibaba-extra-bundle','wait_reset'] yields 3 options — the Extra Bundle step is dropped, and the surviving option reads "Draw on the balance/pack" without saying which. (2) ChatGPT plan's order ['included','prod:codex-credits','prod:codex-saved-reset','wait_reset'] yields 3 options — the SAVED RESET step vanishes, while the same sheet's read-only block two rows below states "Saved resets — 1 banked · expires Sep 1 00:00 EDT" and the Plans widget prose says "One saved reset is banked." The control contradicts the prose. findings.claim: The reference API/catalog price surface does not exist anywhere in the UI, yet three separate UI strings tell the user it does — and one continuation sentence promises billing "at list price" for a list price the user can never see.
findings.detail: A full-DOM scan across all 13 rooms found no "reference API price", no "reference price", no "catalog price", no per-model price row and no $/Mtok pattern. So the axis's check — confirm reference price is Details-only and cannot be read as actual billing — resolves as: unimplemented. That direction is the safe one, but it is falsely advertised as implemented in three places: (1) the Usage-settings sheet note claims "Raw meter policies, source authority, route epochs, probe cadence and price versions live in Advanced/support views"; (2) the Source authority room footnote claims "Route snapshots, receipt refs, pricing versions and source authority live here"; (3) the export intent offers a "Support / analysis bundle — Records plus metadata, source & price versions, redacted receipts." None of the three exists. `meterPolicyVersion` is present in the data on two Z.AI products and has zero renderer references, and there is no pricing-version field at all (see A03-08). Meanwhile prod:zai-credit-plan's whatHappensNext renders "When credits run out, metered continuation applies at list price." Register defect on top: reports/reference-review-report.json marks the packet bullet "confuses reference API price with actual plan settlement" as no-correction-needed / already correct, justified by billingRoute-vs-settlement orthogonality — which answers a different question than the bullet asks and does not address the missing reference-price surface at all.

findings.claim: The Attention room attributes the whole-portfolio blended burn rate to a single API route and measures it against that route's spending limit, producing a warning whose own numbers contradict its own conclusion.
findings.detail: Guard gd-2 renders "Spend rate elevated / Claude API · PAYG / Burn is 2.2× the 7-day norm; still under the org spending limit" with why-rows "burn $2.85/h · norm $1.30/h · limit $150". $2.85/h is byte-identical to costs.burn.perHour, the portfolio-wide blended rate over a $187.42 total of which $125.57 is plan-included valuation that is never billed. The route's own meter reads $6.18 of $150 for the billing cycle — about $0.07/h over the ~91 hours of month-to-date. At the quoted $2.85/h the $150 org limit would be exhausted in roughly 2.2 days, so "still under the org spending limit" cannot be true of the quoted rate. Either the figure is the wrong scope for the card's `where`, or it is an unexplained coincidence; in either reading a user is shown a spend-guard warning built on a number that does not belong to the route it names.

findings.detail: u11-prism.html:851 gates the kind on continuation presence rather than on kind availability: `meters.length + ' meter(s)' + (cont ? ' · ' + p.kind.replace(/_/g,' ') : '')`. findings.claim: The settlement enum is a 4-value subset of canon's closed 6-value settlement_status, and two attempts carry settlement values canon forbids for their state — an INTERRUPTED attempt with partial tokens renders as "settlement settled" and a FAILED attempt as "settlement observed".
findings.detail: Canon B.4 closes settlement_status at observed | streaming_partial | settled | adjusted | failed | unknown. The concept's data uses only four; `adjusted` and `failed` never appear and have zero occurrences anywhere. Two attempts are mis-assigned as a result: ue-520 is status:'interrupted' with real partial tokens (6.2k in / 400 out) yet settlement:'settled', rendered as "Aug 4 · 14:35 EDT · settlement settled" in the attempt list and "Settlement  settled" in the Connection-used grid — canon's aborted/partial-stream unit lists exactly `final_copy` and `settled_copy` as MUST_NOTs; and ue-510 is status:'failed' yet settlement:'observed'. This finding also resolves the axis's collapse question in the concept's favour: settlement was NOT collapsed into billingRoute. The concept split the packet's single "Settlement states" list into two orthogonal fields (billingRoute = what paid; settlement = source quality of the settlement fact), and canon's own reconciliation records that the packet's 7-item list is really canon's cost_status axis and that the packet is internally inconsistent with its own Hermes reference. So the split is the canon-correct move; the defects are the two missing enum values, the two mis-assigned attempts, the un-minted cost_status half (A03-08), and one register hazard: the run detail prints "Settlement" for source quality immediately beneath "Billing route", with no caption, so a reader can easily take "Settlement: observed" for one of the packet's named settlement states.

findings.detail: The eligible-row renderer emits `model.label` and `fm.label + ' · via ' + conn.label` and nothing else identifying (u11-widgets.js:622-624); it never resolves `conn.accountId` to an account label and never resolves the account to its provider family, even though both joins exist in the data (`d.connectionById`, `d.accountById`, `d.familyById` are all available in the same function). findings.axis: AXIS 6 — time and timestamps (re-measured under a non-US zone after the critic flagged the condition was never run)
findings.claim: On any machine whose timezone name contains no slash — including a genuinely UTC host — u11-time.js discards the real zone and silently relabels every timestamp in America/New_York, rendering 75 wrong times per page load.
findings.detail: u11-time.js:20 gates the resolved zone on indexOf('/') !== -1. 'UTC' fails that test, so the resolvable zone is thrown away and the hard-coded America/New_York fallback is used: zoneIsFallback true, U11time.zone = America/New_York. The pinned demo instant 2026-08-04T18:42:00Z then renders as '14:42 EDT' when the honest value is '18:42 UTC' — four hours wrong, across 75 rendered labels per launch. The rule also rejects GMT, Zulu, CET, Japan and Singapore. This is not hypothetical: THE SANDBOX DEFAULT ZONE IS ALREADY UTC, so every '14:42 EDT' string recorded elsewhere in this audit — including the accessible name 'Overview as of 14:42 EDT' captured by the keyboard probe — is this defect firing rather than intended behaviour. Asia/Kolkata is honoured correctly (00:12 GMT+5:30, half-hour offset applied, day rolls to Aug 5), and no 12-hour time appears anywhere in 3 zones x 13 rooms, so the formatter is otherwise sound.
evidence: u11-time.js:20 — zone accepted only when indexOf('/') !== -1

verdicts.reason: The rendering facts are correct (u11-widgets.js:834 emits only ' · v' + op.acquisition.installation.version; targetVersion/arch/failureClass/outcome are never read anywhere — u11-rundetail.js:326 adds only version + provenance; axis8-ops-fieldscan-probe.json confirms '0.43.1', 'x64', 'Target version', 'Outcome' all absent), but the cited rule is misquoted as a mandate. 04_SERVER_NETWORK_MAINTENANCE_AND_DATA_QUALITY.md:58 reads "Provider CLI update detail **may** include:" — permissive. The canon agrees independently: canon/01-reference-canon.md:126 (A8 item 68) says failure class "**may** appear in diagnostics/operation receipts", and item 34 at 01-reference-canon.md:197 is a wording/vocabulary rule sourced to the same P04:60-67 — it cannot be stronger than the 'may' it cites. The Plans citation also does not carry the claim: Plans/usage-feature.md:6249 is a durable-record preservation rule ("Operational records preserve operation_id … status/outcome, times, and partitions …"), and ops-1 does preserve status and outcome as fields (u11-data.js:767); the same sentence's predecessor — "If any such operation invokes a model, the provider attempt gets a separate linked UsageRecord" — is exactly why the provider-active slice lives on ue-609 rather than inside ops-1's phases, so demanding a provider-active partition inside the maintenance record would duplicate the separation the rule mandates. Two sub-claims are also factually wrong: after a rollback the installation IS at v0.42.0, so the acquisition line renders the accurate current version rather than a stale 'pre-update version'; and the missing 'schedule' phase is not a gap, since P04:62 lists a timing vocabulary and this fixture has no scheduled window. refuted_findings.claim: The fixture-19 payload preserves the continuation token but not the originating operation, so ADJ:45 ("preserve the originating operation and its continuation token") is only half satisfied, and the report claims the whole clause.
refuted_findings.detail: ADJ:45 is a two-part requirement. The payload carries continuation:'cont-8841' (the token) but nothing identifying the operation that stalled: no ops-8 id, no workId, no threadId, no run id. ops-8's own record has no work/thread linkage either (workId is not a field on operational entries; the join U11.attemptsOfOperational matches on validationFor/operationalRef, and ops-8 has validationEventId null and no attempt referencing it — attemptsOfOperational('ops-8') returns an empty array). refuted_findings.claim: The cache state enum has no `unknown` value, so an unknown cache state can only be filed as `unsupported` — a positive claim that the route does not cache — and every such row carries a hard-coded `save: 0` that is summed into the displayed "$5.67 Cache saved today" total; combined with cache-read/cache-write counts never being rendered and no reported-zero row existing, GUI-USG-006 is unmeetable on every MUST clause and this axis cannot be certified.
refuted_findings.detail: Plans canon §B.9 instructs the audit to score the three GUI-USG-006 fixture values (`reported` / `not_exposed` / `unknown`) plus the rule "reported cache_read = 0 != unsupported/not_exposed/unknown". The concept's cacheStats carries `state: measured | estimated | unsupported` (probe P1: cacheStatesPresent = ["estimated","measured","unsupported"]). That triad is legitimately UF-081's view requirement — the concept's own research names it at research/plans-usage-synthesis.md:47-48 — but it is used as the ONLY cache provenance axis, replacing UF-080's `cache_reporting_state` and `cache_miss_reason`, which appear nowhere in the concept (grep across u11-*.js/html: 0 hits; the only repo hits are in research/, which correctly quotes the requirement). Three consequences, each independently verified: (i) there is no `unknown` cache state, so a route whose cache support PM does not know must be typed `unsupported`, which the UI renders as the definite sentence "Route does not support prompt cache markers"; (ii) both `unsupported` rows carry `save: 0` (probe P1 cacheRowsWithZeroSave = conn:zai-legacy, conn:antigravity-cli), and u11-widgets.js:489 / u11-prism.html:718 / u11-prism.html:1408 all sum `s + (cs.save || 0)` over ALL eight rows, so an unsupported (or misfiled-unknown) route contributes a definite $0.00 to the headline savings figure the user reads — the MUST_NOT `unsupported_cache_as_zero` in spirit; (iii) no row has `cr: 0` (probe P1 cacheRowsWithReportedZeroRead = 0) and renderCache never reads cs.cr or cs.cw at all, so the positive arm — a reported cache_read of 0 rendered distinctly from unsupported — has no fixture and no renderer. The concept's own register makes this worse rather than better: reports/candidate-dry-delta.json:44 describes the shipped cacheStats as "(provider-reported vs derived vs not exposed)", an axis the code does not implement.

verdicts.corrected_claim: The concept defines no cache-state enum in code at all — renderCache (u11-widgets.js:888) branches only on the literal 'unsupported'; the closed-looking triad is the fixture's, not a declared enum (an injected state:'unknown' would fall into the else-branch and render as an ordinary measured row, calling cs.save.toFixed(2)). Also, part (ii) is weaker than stated on its own: for a route that genuinely does not support prompt caching, save:0 is arithmetically correct, so the $5.67 total is only wrong conditional on the missing unknown/not_exposed state forcing an unknown route into 'unsupported'. refuted_findings.claim: Of the eight cache records 02_*.md:79-88 requires, three are absent from the concept entirely (predicted impact; invalidation/reduced-reuse reason at the connection level; a per-field provider-reported/derived/estimated source that is actually shown), and the two token records are present in data but rendered in no cache surface.
refuted_findings.detail: Full map against the packet's list, data vs UI kept distinct. (1) Predicted impact — ABSENT from data and UI; no surface predicts a cache consequence before an action. `predicted` appears in u11-data.js only as `predictedSustainable` in the capacity block (probe P1: predictedCacheKeys = []). The nearest thing is the post-hoc `cacheEffect` (rebuilt/preserved/broken/unknown) on maintenance records and the no-gain scenario's "Would reclaim ~0 tokens", which predicts context reclaim, not cache. (2) ContextEpoch — present but self-contradictory, see A05-05. (3) Stable-prefix identity — present for thread t-88 only, see A05-06. (4) Actual cache-read tokens — in data (`cr` on 6 of 8 rows) and rendered in NO cache surface (probe P3: mentionsCacheReadTokens = false in the cache room); cacheRead does render per-attempt in the ledger and attempt detail, but that is a different record than the per-connection cache figure the packet's Cache section governs. A value type such as ToolRecoveryEnvelope is not a service." All 18 packet role names have 0 occurrences anywhere in Plans/** (UsageEventStore, UsageNormalizer, SettlementResolver, UsageDataQuality, UsageForecast, CapacityProjection, RouteReceipt, CacheReceipt, TimeBreakdown, ProviderFamilyUsage, AccountConnectionUsage, HelperPurposeGroup, MaintenanceActivity, ContextUsageDetail, RunOutProjection, SourceFreshness, UsageWidgetHost — each grep = 0), so by that rule none of them becomes a service and all stay with their existing domain owners. candidate-dry-delta.json instead marks 16 'present' + 1 'present-new' + 1 'gap' and never cites DRY_Rules.md; and none of the 16 canonical service names (RuntimeResourceGovernor, ObservableWork, InstallationResolver, InstallationLifecycleManager, ThreadCommandOutbox, ProjectionReplayCoordinator, EnvironmentConnectionSupervisor, BackSeatDriverService, OperationalAwarenessService, ...) appears in any report or source file of the concept. Roles that map directly onto named shared services and are therefore misdirected: CapacityProjection (runs[].capacity admission envelope) -> RuntimeResourceGovernor, 'Shared policy/admission with enforcement on the exact Execution Host' (DRY_Rules.md:2089, prohibited peer 'per-feature scheduler/admission governor'); MaintenanceActivity (operational[] phases/status/outcome) -> ObservableWork, 'Shared truthful phase, wait, progress, cancellation, and outcome projection' (:2090, prohibited peer 'feature-local work/progress state machine') and InstallationLifecycleManager (:2083) / InstallationResolver (:2082) for the ops-1/ops-8 acquisition lifecycle; ops-2 offline_outbox -> ThreadCommandOutbox (:2086); reconnect replay -> ProjectionReplayCoordinator (:2087); bsdEvents -> BackSeatDriverService (:2097), whose boundary already names Usage as retaining only presentation. Plans/CLI_Bridged_Providers.md:1499 spells this out for the exact ops-1 flow the concept demonstrates: 'InstallationLifecycleManager decides retry budget, backoff, circuit state, cooldown ...; ObservableWork projects the truthful wait and outcome.' Independently, the claimed u11 owners are mostly not modules or functions: 13 of the 17 resolve to data fields or enums (SettlementResolver = 'billingRoute ... orthogonal to settlement'; UsageDataQuality = 'meter vs values ... + conf + note'; RouteReceipt = 'attempts[].receiptRef'; CacheReceipt = 'tokens.cacheRead/cacheWrite'; TimeBreakdown = 'runs[].timing.rows'; ProviderFamilyUsage = 'costs.byFamily'; HelperPurposeGroup = 'buckets{} + taxonomy'; Goal/CrewUsage = 'runs[] + members[]'; MaintenanceActivity = 'operational[]'; SourceFreshness = 'meta.projectionHealth/projectionFreshness'; CapacityProjection = 'runs[].capacity'; UsageForecast = 'forecasts[]'; UsageNormalizer = 'sourceClass + settlement fields'). Only four have real code behind them: UsageEventStore (U11.attemptById, u11-data.js:1195), AccountConnectionUsage (accountsOfFamily :1203 / connectionsOfAccount :1206), ContextUsageDetail (u11-context.js) and UsageWidgetHost (see A11-12). RunOutProjection is correctly flagged as a gap with a legitimate pointer — FINDINGS.md:50-56 does contain the run-out finding registered as U1.

refuted_findings.claim: The provider-CLI correction review never opened the canonical owner doc, which already encodes the adjudication and already normalizes the exact tokens the concept then invented: 'setup_required' vs canonical 'provider_setup_required', and 'verify_failed' vs canonical 'generation_verification_failed'.
refuted_findings.detail: Plans/CLI_Bridged_Providers.md already carries the adjudication as active canon: :1465 'No provider CLI is bundled in Puppet Master core ... or silently acquired by Project/model/provider/Goal/Plan/WorkNode/agent/Auto/On demand'; :1466 explicit user-triggered Install/Setup from an official source for the exact Host/Environment; :1507 records that packet-root PROVIDER_CLI_FINAL_ADJUDICATION.md supersedes only the permissive clauses; :1529 'Missing provider CLI demand returns typed provider_setup_required with exact Host/Environment and continuation evidence and never silently installs or cross-routes'; :1569 'Do not bundle, baseline, pre-seed, mirror/repackage by default, or silently acquire a provider CLI'; and :1499 fixes the normalized lifecycle failure classes (installation_owner_unknown, wrong_install_target, ..., generation_verification_failed, rollback_unsupported, rollback_failed). The concept instead uses non-canonical tokens: operational kind and outcome 'setup_required' (u11-data.js:803, declared as the new kind in event-schema-delta.json new_collections) where the canonical typed return is 'provider_setup_required' (which exists in CLI_Bridged_Providers.md, plan_units.jsonl and acceptance_units.jsonl); and failureClass 'verify_failed' on ops-1 (u11-data.js:767) where the canonical class is 'generation_verification_failed'. This breaches SHARED_PROCESS_RULES.md ('Preserve source terminology and owner boundaries'; 'Reuse canonical owners, commands, wiring paths, DRY services, events, receipts, and schemas') and 00_READ_ME_FIRST.md ('Do not claim the work was already covered without exact evidence'). Note the three correction-packet sha256 values the report cites ARE correct — I verified them byte-for-byte; the defect is which sources were opened, not the hashes.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Plans/CLI_Bridged_Providers.md:1465 ('No provider CLI is bundled in Puppet Master core… or silently acquired by Project/model/provider/Goal/Plan/WorkNode/agent/`Auto`/`On` demand'), :1466 (explicit user-triggered Install/Setup, official source, exact Host/Environment), :1507 (packet-root PROVIDER_CLI_FINAL_ADJUDICATION.md supersedes only the permissive clauses), :1529 ('Missing provider CLI demand returns typed provider_setup_required with exact Host/Environment and continuation evidence…'), :1569 and :1499 all read as quoted. Token grounding: `grep -rlF provider_setup_required Plans/` hits CLI_Bridged_Providers.md, its _shards mirror, a ledgers design_atoms.jsonl and Plans/.plan_index/{plan_units,acceptance_units}.jsonl — so the finding's file list is accurate; `grep -rF verify_failed Plans/` returns 0; generation_verification_failed hits CLI_Bridged_Providers.md. The concept uses u11-data.js:767 failureClass: 'verify_failed' and :803 outcome: 'setup_required' (kind 'setup_required' likewise), and `grep -rn provider_setup_required` over the entire concept returns 0. reports/reference-review-report.json sources_opened is exactly 15 entries — four correction-packet files, SOURCE_AND_PRECEDENCE_MAP.md, and ten Concepts/QwenUsageConcept paths — with zero Plans/** entries, while its policy_audit adjudicates the CLI acquisition rules ('corrected' / 'no-correction-needed') item by item.

Both halves fail. (a) The packet the correction was run against contains neither token: grep over PM_Usage_Dependency_and_Work_Correction_2026-08-13/ returns 0 hits for provider_setup_required, setup_required, generation_verification_failed and verify_failed; its only requirement is the user-facing string at PROVIDER_CLI_FINAL_ADJUDICATION.md:43 "return Provider Setup Required when none is ready", which u11-data.js:806 renders exactly. (b) Plans/CLI_Bridged_Providers.md did not "already" encode this: the cited clauses sit inside the "Remaining Runtime Integration Addendum - Provider CLI Lifecycle Consumer (2026-08-13)" (heading at :1459) sourced from a different packet, PM_Remaining_Runtime_Integration_Final_CORRECTED_2026-08-13 (:1552-1560), and `git show b2e5ae7ab8:Plans/CLI_Bridged_Providers.md` (2026-08-10, 1630 lines) has zero occurrences of provider_setup_required or generation_verification_failed — both landed with 880bbd942a on 2026-08-15, after the concept's 2026-08-13 correction. The "never opened Plans" root cause also fails for the concept as a whole: candidate-command-delta.json's census cites Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md UCC-116, Plans/Wiring_Matrix.production.json, Plans/Multi-Account.md:5088 and Plans/FinalGUISpec.md, and candidate-dry-delta.json records "No canonical RunOutProjection definition exists in Plans/**".
verdicts.corrected_claim: At most an info-level observation: reference-review-report.json's sources_opened lists 15 paths and none under Plans/**, so the 2026-08-13 correction review is documented as a packet-plus-concept review only; but the concept's internal field values setup_required and verify_failed cannot be scored against Plans tokens that entered the repo from a different packet on or after the same day, and the packet's own required string ("Provider Setup Required") is rendered verbatim.

refuted_findings.claim: ue-609, the Codex CLI update's verification call, is parented to an unrelated user turn, so the Ledger and Context Details attribute maintenance usage to "Run integration tests" while two other surfaces say the same event is validation and "never user work".
refuted_findings.detail:
ue-609 carries `workId: 'work-4'` and `validationFor: 'ops-1'` (u11-data.js:698-705). work-4 is the user turn "Run integration tests" (u11-data.js:312). One event, four contradictory presentations:
- Ledger: work-4's card reads "15.3k input · 900 output · 7.7k cache read · 1 helper call" — that "1 helper call" IS the CLI-update verification probe; at Advanced it appears as a row inside the user turn ("Validation & probes | probe | completed | 1.5k input · 210 output").
- Context Details: the same probe is listed among the attempts of the "Run integration tests" turn.
- Source authority room: the same event renders "Active probe · Qwen3 Coder Plus / 1.5k input · 210 output · attributed to validation, never user work" (u11-widgets.js:948-955).
- Attempt drawer: "Verification call for maintenance 'Codex CLI update' — the installer time is not usage; this call is." (u11-rundetail.js:315-322).
The concept handles the other probe correctly: ue-620 carries `workId: null` and is excluded from every ledger group (verified: 42 of 45 attempts are in a ledger group; the three outside are ue-620, ue-091, ue-092). So the two probes are treated inconsistently and maintenance usage is attributed to a user turn. Counting itself is clean — ue-609 is counted exactly once, and the Maintenance & operations card renders no token or cost figures at all (a digit scan of that widget returned []).

Validation & probes / probe / completed / 1.5k input · 210 output'); renderAuthority at u11-widgets.js:947-953 emits '· attributed to validation, never user work ·' for the same event; u11-rundetail.js:315-322 renders 'Verification call for maintenance ... the installer time is not usage; this call is.'; and the operations card carries no token/cost digits, only 'View the verification call' (probe2-out.json opsWidget[0]). ue-620 (u11-data.js:598) correctly carries workId:null. verdicts.corrected_claim: Lead with a stronger, in-concept citation than the packet: reports/event-schema-delta.json attempt_schema.core defines workId as 'logical work join (works[].id) | null for pure validation'. ue-609 is pure validation (validationFor:'ops-1', bucket 'validation', purpose 'probe') yet carries workId:'work-4', so the concept violates its own published schema; ue-620 (workId:null) complies. That makes the inconsistency self-evident without needing packet 04's looser wording.

verdicts.reason: The facts are right but the cited rules do not forbid the behaviour. 04_SERVER_NETWORK_MAINTENANCE_AND_DATA_QUALITY.md:53 says only 'If a maintenance flow invokes a model for verification, that provider call is a separate `validation` event' — and ue-609 (u11-data.js:698) is exactly that: bucket 'validation', purpose 'probe', validationFor 'ops-1', rendered on every surface with its validation identity intact ('Validation & probes | probe' in the ledger, 'attributed to validation, never user work' in u11-widgets.js:948-955). Live canon A54 (ORG:412 / HER:527 / P04:104) requires probes be attributed 'as probe/validation usage rather than user work', which the concept does — grouping under a logical turn is a different axis from purpose attribution. The other cited rule cuts the opposite way: 02_EVENTS_ROUTES_HELPERS_CACHE_AND_CONTEXT.md:25 requires every real attempt to be 'grouped under one logical turn', so work-4 membership satisfies it and ue-620's `workId: null` (u11-data.js:598) is the row that breaches it. The finding itself concedes counting is clean (ue-609 counted once, the operations card carries no token or cost digits — I confirmed the ops widget renders only the 'View the verification call' link). What is left is the 'helper call' mislabel on the Essentials card, which is already A04-05's defect, plus a data-modelling inconsistency between the two probes with no rule against either.
